toolbar.signals.tooltip: Signals (A): Click a crossing to see its approaches, lanes and movements in the colours of their signal groups. On a junction made in this project, add, rename and remove signal groups and give each movement its group.
signals.click_junction: Click a crossing in the map.
signals.status.start: Click a crossing to see its signal groups and movements.
signals.status.target: Crossing #{id}: {approaches} approaches, {movements} movements, {groups, plural, =0 {no signal groups} one {# signal group} other {# signal groups}}. Click a movement or choose its group in the panel.
signals.junction: Crossing #{id}: {approaches} approaches, {movements} movements, {groups, plural, =0 {no signal groups} one {# signal group} other {# signal groups}}
signals.owner.made: Made in this project: the signal groups and movements can be changed.
signals.owner.mismatch: Made in this project, but its file does not match the junction it was made as any more; make it again (for example with the markings tool) before changing its signals.
signals.owner.readonly: Made in this project; signals can only be changed on the base map of a project.
signals.owner.omsi: This crossing comes with OMSI: its signals are shown as they are. Signals can be changed on junctions made in this project.
signals.group.add.tooltip: Adds a signal group that is red for the whole cycle; give movements this group in the list below.
signals.approach: Approach {n} ({lanes, plural, one {# lane} other {# lanes}})
signals.group.name.tooltip: Light number {n} in the crossing's program; the heads of this group name it in their first label.
signals.group.count: {count, plural, =0 {no movements} one {# movement} other {# movements}}
signals.shared_lane: Shared lane: these movements stop at the same line and switch together.
signals.several_lights: This movement passes more than one stop line with different signal groups.
signals.plan.readonly: Shown as OMSI's file has it; nothing here can be changed.
signals.plan.point: Click a movement in the map or in the list.
signals.status.none_here: There is no crossing with at least two approaches here.
signals.done.renamed: Signal group renamed to {name} on junction #{id}
signals.status.heads_show: {count, plural, one {# signal head shows} other {# signal heads show}} group {name}; move them to another group first.
signals.done.unassigned: {text} now has no signal on junction #{id}
signals.status.lost: {count, plural, one {# movement is} other {# movements are}} gone from the junction made anew and lost {count, plural, one {its} other {their}} signal group.
signals.cycle.tooltip: How long one cycle of the program lasts, in seconds; every group starts again after it.
signals.state.tooltip: What the group shows during the selected stretch
signals.segment.start.tooltip: Second at which the stretch starts
signals.segment.length.tooltip: How many seconds the stretch lasts
signals.segment.remove.tooltip: Removes the selected stretch; the one before it takes its time.
signals.segment.repeat.tooltip: Repeats the selected stretch straight after itself; what follows moves on.
signals.timeline.hint: Drag along a row to paint that stretch of time in the chosen colour; drag the edge between two stretches to move it (Shift: tenths of a second).
signals.segment.split.tooltip: Cuts the selected stretch where you clicked it (or in its middle) and paints the part after the cut in the chosen colour.
signals.status.brush_pedestrian: {group} is a pedestrian light: it shows only red and green.
signals.status.split_same: The stretch is already {colour}: choose another colour to paint with; the part after the cut takes it.
signals.status.split_short: This stretch is too short to split.
signals.discard.tooltip: Forgets the changes of the timeline since the last Apply.
signals.apply.tooltip: Writes the changed timeline into the junction, as one step that Ctrl+Z takes back.
signals.timeline.empty: No signal groups yet; add one on the Movements tab.
signals.timeline.pick: Click a stretch to change its colour, start or length.
signals.segment: {group}: {start} to {end} s{holds, select, yes { (holds to the end of the cycle)} other {}}
signals.check.beyond: {group} has phases after {seconds} s that the cycle never reaches.
signals.check.empty: {group} has an empty phase at {seconds} s.
signals.check.green_red: {group} goes from green straight to red at {seconds} s, without yellow.
signals.check.red_green: {group} goes from red straight to green at {seconds} s, without red and yellow.
signals.check.pedestrian: {group} is for pedestrians, whose heads show only red and green, but shows another value at {seconds} s.
signals.check.hold: A stop or jump point at {seconds} s lies outside the cycle or names no group.
signals.status.discarded: The changes of the timeline were not applied and are gone.
signals.status.bad_seconds: Type a number of seconds, 0 or more.
signals.phases.empty: This junction has no signal groups yet. The assistant proposes groups and a cycle.
signals.phases.none: This program does not run in whole phases: its groups change at different times or show other signals. Below, when which groups may go; it is edited on the timeline, so nothing is lost.
signals.phases.info: Phases: {count} · cycle {cycle} s. Click a group to let it go in a phase or not.
signals.phases.readonly: Phases: {count} · cycle {cycle} s. Shown only: the signals of this crossing cannot be changed here.
signals.phases.add.tooltip: Adds a phase at the end, for the groups no phase has yet.
signals.phases.up.tooltip: Moves this phase up by one.
signals.phases.chip.on: {group} goes in this phase; click to take it out.
signals.phases.chip.off: {group} waits in this phase; click to let it go.
signals.phases.status.last_group: A phase needs at least one group.
signals.phases.status.invalid: These times do not make a cycle: every phase needs green time.
signals.phases.status.merged: Two phases in a row would let the same groups go and run into one; change the groups of one of them first.
signals.wizard.title: Signal assistant
signals.wizard.open.tooltip: Proposes signal groups and a basic program for this junction, checked for conflicts.
signals.wizard.offer: No signals yet: the assistant proposes groups, a cycle and heads in a few steps.
signals.wizard.analysis: Approaches: {approaches} · lanes: {lanes} · vehicle movements: {movements} · groups now: {groups} · heads: {heads}
signals.wizard.separate_left: Left-turn lanes get a phase of their own
signals.wizard.separate_left.tooltip: On: left turns from lanes of their own go in a phase of their own and need not give way. Off: they go with the straight traffic and give way to oncoming vehicles.
signals.wizard.check.free: Conflict-free: no movements that cross or join without giving way go at the same time. Turning movements that give way: {permitted}.
signals.wizard.check.conflicts: Not conflict-free: movements that cross or join go at the same time ({count}).
signals.wizard.check.footpaths: Footpaths that cross lanes get no lights from the assistant: {count}.
signals.wizard.replaces: Use replaces the groups of this junction ({count}).
signals.wizard.heads_kept: Heads already there keep their group numbers ({count}); check them under Signal heads.
signals.wizard.heads.tooltip: Places a head for every group at each approach it serves, at the stop line, with the junction as variable parent; openOMSI runs a program only with heads.
signals.heads.type.tooltip: An object of your installation with [trafficlight]; heads already used in this map come first.
signals.heads.height.tooltip: How high above the junction the heads hang. A head object is only the signal: put a pole or mast of your own beneath it.
signals.wizard.back.tooltip: Closes the assistant without changing anything.
signals.wizard.use.tooltip: Writes the groups, the program and the heads into the junction as one step; Ctrl+Z takes it back.
signals.wizard.confirm: Click again to replace the groups ({count})
signals.done.wizard: Junction #{id}: the assistant’s groups ({groups}) and cycle of {cycle} s are written.
signals.done.wizard_heads: Junction #{id}: the assistant’s groups ({groups}), cycle of {cycle} s and heads are written.
signals.heads.none: No signal heads name this crossing.
signals.heads.none_warning: No signal heads name this crossing: openOMSI runs its program only when a head has the crossing as variable parent.
signals.heads.group.tooltip: The group this head shows: its first label. Only the head in the map changes, so this works at OMSI’s own crossings too.
signals.heads.place.tooltip: Places a head for every group without one at each approach it serves, with the head type and height of the assistant.
signals.heads.status.no_types: No signal head objects ([trafficlight]) were found in this installation.
signals.heads.status.place_failed: Heads that could not be placed: {count} (see the log).
signals.heads.mast.tooltip: The object each head hangs on, placed under it. Masts found under heads in this map come first (or, in a map without heads, those of another map of your installation, such as Grundorf) and stand to their head as there.
signals.heads.mast_search.tooltip: Type part of a file name to choose any object of your installation as mast.
signals.heads.place_with: With head {head}, mast {mast}, height {height} m (set in the assistant).
signals.check.nothing: This crossing has no signal groups to check.
signals.check.summary: Errors: {errors} · warnings: {warnings} · hints: {hints} (conflicts between movements found: {conflicts})
signals.check.summary_clean: No errors or warnings · hints: {hints} (conflicts between movements found: {conflicts})
signals.check.exceptions_note: Manual exceptions: {count}. They are your decision, not something the check proved safe.
signals.matrix.cell: {first} × {second}: {relation} (conflicting movements: {conflicts}); green together for {together} s a cycle
signals.matrix.manual: Manual exception: allowed to go together by you.
signals.matrix.click_add: Click to allow these groups to go together (a manual exception).
signals.matrix.click_remove: Click to take the manual exception back.
signals.done.exception_added: Junction #{id}: {first} and {second} may go together (manual exception).
signals.done.exception_removed: Junction #{id}: the manual exception for {first} and {second} is taken back.
signals.finding.crossing: {first} and {second} are green together from {seconds} s for {length} s, and their paths cross.
signals.finding.merging: {first} and {second} are green together from {seconds} s for {length} s, and their traffic joins one lane.
signals.finding.pedestrian: {first} and {second} are green together from {seconds} s for {length} s, and straight traffic crosses a footpath.
signals.finding.conditional: {first} and {second} go together; turning traffic gives way.
signals.finding.within: Movements of {group} meet each other; no program can keep them apart.
signals.finding.exception: {first} and {second} are green together for {length} s, allowed by your manual exception.
signals.finding.intergreen: Only {length} s from the end of {first} at {seconds} s to the green of {second} (at least {least} s).
signals.finding.head_group: Heads showing group {n}, which the program does not have: {count}.
signals.finding.no_head: {group} has no head: openOMSI shows its traffic nothing.
signals.finding.dark: {group} goes dark from {seconds} s: the crossing is unsignalled then and its signs count.
signals.preview.play.tooltip: Play or pause the preview. It runs the program as openOMSI does and changes no file.
signals.preview.restart.tooltip: Back to the start of the cycle.
signals.preview.forward.tooltip: One second on (stop and jump points count).
signals.preview.time.tooltip: The second of the cycle the preview is at; type one to jump there.
signals.preview.loop.tooltip: On: the cycle starts again. Off: one cycle, then the preview pauses.
signals.preview.request.tooltip: Somebody asks for {group}: stop and jump points waiting for it act as in openOMSI.
signals.templates.open.tooltip: Keeps the program of this crossing as a template, or applies one: two phases, four arms, T junction, separate left turns, a crossing on request, or your own.
signals.templates.title: Templates
signals.templates.info: Crossing with {approaches} approaches and {movements} vehicle movements; signal groups now: {groups}. Choose a template: arm and turn decide which movement gets which group.
signals.templates.info_readonly: Crossing with {approaches} approaches and {movements} vehicle movements; signal groups now: {groups}. This crossing is only read: a template can be kept from it, but not applied to it.
signals.templates.user_none: None yet. Name the program of a crossing below to keep it.
signals.templates.facts: Needs {arms} arms and {groups} signal groups; cycle {cycle} s.
signals.templates.fit.ok: Fits this crossing: every movement has a group and every group has movements.
signals.templates.fit.arms: The template needs {needed} arms, the crossing has {have}.
signals.templates.fit.empty: No movement of this crossing for: {names}.
signals.templates.fit.contested: Movements claimed by two groups (the first one has them): {count}.
signals.templates.fit.unlit: Movements that get no signal and would never stop: {count}.
signals.templates.fit.footpaths: Footpaths have no signal groups and stay as they are.
signals.templates.correct: Choose a group for what does not fit
signals.templates.apply.tooltip: Writes the template's groups, program and bindings into the junction as one step; Ctrl+Z takes it back. Missing heads are placed if chosen below.
signals.templates.confirm.replace: Click again to replace the groups ({count})
signals.templates.confirm.unfitting: Click again: movements without a signal ({unlit})
signals.templates.back.tooltip: Closes the templates without changing anything.
signals.templates.save.title: Keep this crossing's program
signals.templates.save.name: Name
signals.templates.save.name.tooltip: The name of the template. It is kept as a file in Documents\OMSI MapWorks\Signal templates and can be used on any map.
signals.templates.save.tooltip: Keeps the groups, the times and what each group controls (by arm and turn, without object IDs) as a template.
signals.templates.save.overwrite: Click again to replace the template
signals.templates.delete.tooltip: Deletes this template file. The programs of crossings are not touched.
signals.templates.done: Template {name} applied to crossing #{id}: signal groups {groups}.
signals.templates.heads_hint: Heads are not changed: place them with the heads button below (groups without a head: {count}).
signals.templates.status.load_problems: Template files in {folder} that could not be read: {count}. The log names them.
signals.templates.status.nothing: This crossing has no signal groups to keep.
signals.templates.status.no_name: Give the template a name first.
signals.templates.status.dirty: Apply or discard the changes in the phases or the timeline first: a template keeps what is applied.
signals.templates.status.save_failed: The template could not be written: {reason}
signals.templates.status.imprecise: Movements that could not be told apart from others of the same arm and turn: {count}. The template gives them one group.
signals.template.two_phase.desc: Arms 1 and 3 go together, then arms 2 and 4; left turns go with the rest and give way. For a crossroads.
signals.template.four_arms.desc: Every arm has a phase of its own, one after the other. For a crossroads; no turn meets another.
signals.template.t_junction.desc: Every arm of three has a phase of its own, one after the other.
signals.template.separate_left.desc: Arms 1 and 3 go, then their left turns from lanes of their own, then arms 2 and 4 and their left turns. For a crossroads with left-turn lanes.
signals.template.pedestrian_request.desc: Two arms: green until somebody asks (a request point), then yellow, red for people to cross, and green again. Footpaths cannot be bound to a light.
signals.templates.heads.tooltip: Places a head for each group that has none, with the head type, height and mast of the assistant. Off: heads stay as they are.
signals.wizard.foot: Crossings get a light of their own
signals.wizard.foot.tooltip: On: each footpath over an arm that vehicles cross gets a light, green with the phases where no vehicle crosses it and turning vehicles give way, or in a phase of its own. Off: crossings get no light.
signals.finding.pedestrian_window: {group}: green for only {seconds}, but people need about {needed} s to cross; nobody starts across it
